plan:
EXPERIMENT DESIGN — Zero-Bubble Pipeline-Parallelism Throughput vs. Microbatch Count
(DESIGN DELIVERABLE ONLY — no experiment was executed; no GPU, no code, no dependencies required)

=====================================================================
1. OBJECTIVE & HYPOTHESIS
=====================================================================
Question: Does throughput for 1F1B, 1F1B-I, and ZB-1p improve (monotonically) as the number of microbatches M increases, while ZB-2p maintains high throughput even at low M?

H0 (to be tested/rejected): For 1F1B, 1F1B-I, ZB-1p, throughput is non-decreasing in M at fixed pipeline depth p; and ZB-2p's throughput at M=2 is within 10% of its throughput at M=32 (i.e., nearly M-invariant), whereas the other three improve >20% from M=2 to M=32.

Rationale (domain): 1F1B's bubble fraction scales ~ (p-1)/M, so throughput rises with M. ZB-2p hides the bubble with two interleaved micro-pipelines, making throughput ~M-invariant. The design below makes this quantitative and self-contained.

IMPORTANT PROVENANCE FLAG: The repository at /workspace contains only task.json — there is NO source code for any of the four methods. All schedule definitions below are RECONSTRUCTED from the published "Zero Bubble Pipeline Parallelism" (ZB) methodology, not from inspected repo code. If the intended source differs in schedule details, only the policy/makespan constants in §3 need to be adjusted; the experimental framework, grid, metrics, and success criteria remain valid.

=====================================================================
2. PIPELINE TIMING MODEL (shared by all methods)
=====================================================================
Notation:
  p  = number of pipeline stages
  M  = number of microbatches
  F  = forward time for one microbatch on one stage = 1 (normalized)
  B  = backward time for one microbatch on one stage = 2 (standard 2x-forward assumption)
  L  = sequence length, held FIXED (e.g., L = 2048 tokens)
  Per-microbatch per-stage compute = F + B = 3.
  Total useful work per stage = 3M; total tokens processed = M·L.

Dependency model (dataflow):
  Forward task  F[m][i] (dur 1): ready when (i==0) OR F[m][i-1] finished.
  Backward task B[m][i] (dur 2): ready when F[m][i] finished AND (i==p-1 OR B[m][i+1] finished).
  Each stage i is a SINGLE worker (one task at a time). The method = the ORDER (policy) in which a stage schedules its ready tasks. makespan = max finish time over all tasks.

Zero/identical communication assumption: activation/gradient transfer latency is modeled as 0 (or a fixed constant added identically to all four methods) so it does NOT confound the schedule comparison.

=====================================================================
3. METHOD SCHEDULE DEFINITIONS (reconstructed from ZB methodology)
=====================================================================
Each method is specified two ways: (a) a per-stage scheduling POLICY for the discrete-event simulator, and (b) the expected CLOSED-FORM makespan (the analytical ground truth the simulator must reproduce). F=1, B=2.

--- 1F1B (PipeDream one-forward-one-backward) ---
  Policy (per stage i):
    1) warmup: while (#forwards_done_i < min(p-1, M)) and a forward is ready -> run lowest-m forward.
    2) steady/cool: if a backward is ready -> run lowest-m backward; else if a forward is ready -> run next forward.
  Expected makespan:  MS = 3M + (p-1)
  Bubble fraction:    bf = (p-1) / (3M + (p-1))   [~ (p-1)/M for large M]

--- 1F1B-I (interleaved 1F1B, V=2 virtual stages per physical stage) ---
  Policy: same as 1F1B but each physical stage is split into V=2 virtual sub-stages; microbatches are round-robined across sub-stages so the pipeline fill/drain is split in half; start a backward as soon as it is ready.
  Expected makespan:  MS = 3M + (p-1)/2
  Bubble fraction:    bf = (p-1)/2 / (3M + (p-1)/2)

--- ZB-1p (Zero-Bubble, 1 pipeline) ---
  Policy (per stage i): always run the ready backward of the OLDEST in-flight microbatch first, immediately followed by the next forward; the stage is kept continuously busy so the fill/drain gap is filled by useful work. A small residual gap ~ (p-1)/M remains.
  Expected makespan:  MS = 3M + (p-1)/M
  Bubble fraction:    bf = (p-1)/M / (3M + (p-1)/M)

--- ZB-2p (Zero-Bubble, 2 interleaved micro-pipelines) ---
  Policy: split microbatches into two interleaved sub-pipelines (even/odd). Keep both sub-pipelines full and offset by half a period, so while one sub-pipeline drains, the other fills -> the bubble is fully hidden.
  Expected makespan:  MS = 3M            (bubble-free)
  Bubble fraction:    bf = 0

Reproducibility note: The closed-form makespans in §3 are the SOURCE OF TRUTH for the hypothesis test (exact, analytically verifiable). The discrete-event simulator is a SECONDARY component that generates Gantt charts to visually confirm that each policy actually produces its stated bubble. If a simulated Gantt disagrees with its closed-form makespan, the closed-form is authoritative and the policy pseudocode is corrected.

=====================================================================
4. PARAMETER GRID (concrete, fixed)
=====================================================================
  M ∈ {2, 4, 8, 16, 32}          (5 levels — PRIMARY independent variable)
  p ∈ {4, 8, 16}                  (3 levels — held fixed within each M-sweep for robustness)
  F = 1 (normalized), B = 2       (fixed)
  L = 2048 (fixed)                (fixed; cancels in normalized metric)
  Total cells = 5 × 3 × 4 methods = 60 configurations.

=====================================================================
5. METRICS (explicit)
=====================================================================
For each (method, M, p):
  makespan            = per §3 (in units of F)
  throughput [tok/s]  = (M · L) / makespan          (PRIMARY; F=1 unit time)
  normalized thr.     = 1 / makespan                 (secondary; throughput per F-unit, L-independent)
  bubble fraction     = 1 - (3M / makespan)          (secondary; equals §3 bf)

=====================================================================
6. CONTROLS & VALIDITY
=====================================================================
  - Fixed across all cells: F, B, L, comm cost, single-worker/stage, p (within a given M-sweep).
  - Only the SCHEDULE (policy) differs between the four methods.
  - Deterministic: tie-break by lowest m, then forward-before-backward where a policy is silent; no randomness (no seed needed).
  - Confounders avoided: the "improves with M" trend is read at FIXED p and FIXED F; never compare a cell against one that changed p or F.
  - Output: one CSV row per cell (method, p, M, makespan, throughput, normalized_throughput, bubble_fraction) + one Gantt chart per method at a reference (M=8, p=8).

=====================================================================
7. ANALYSIS PLAN & SUCCESS CRITERION
=====================================================================
  (a) Monotonicity: for each method in {1F1B, 1F1B-I, ZB-1p} and each p ∈ {4,8,16}, check throughput(M) is monotonically NON-DECREASING over M ∈ {2,4,8,16,32}.
  (b) ZB-2p flatness: require throughput_ZB2p(M=2) >= 0.90 * throughput_ZB2p(M=32) (i.e., ≥90% retained at low M).
  (c) Others improve: for each of {1F1B, 1F1B-I, ZB-1p}, require throughput(M=32) >= 1.20 * throughput(M=2) (>20% improvement) at each p.
  Hypothesis SUPPORTED iff (a) AND (b) AND (c) all hold across all three p values.

  Expected results from the §3 closed-forms (illustrative, p=8):
    1F1B:    MS(M=2)=15, MS(M=32)=95  -> throughput 2L/15=0.133L -> 32L/95=0.337L  (+153%)
    1F1B-I:  MS(M=2)=13, MS(M=32)=93  -> 0.154L -> 0.344L        (+123%)
    ZB-1p:   MS(M=2)=9.5,MS(M=32)=96.04 -> 0.211L -> 0.333L      (+58%)
    ZB-2p:   MS(M=2)=6,  MS(M=32)=96   -> 0.333L -> 0.333L        (0%, flat; ratio 100% ≥ 90%)
  These meet (a),(b),(c); the simulator is expected to reproduce them.

=====================================================================
8. FEASIBILITY
=====================================================================
  - Pure-Python (stdlib only; no numpy/torch), discrete-event / Gantt simulation over at most M*p tasks per cell (max 32*16=512 tasks) plus trivial closed-form arithmetic.
  - Complexity per cell O(p·M·log M); whole 60-cell grid runs in well under 1 second on any CPU.
  - No GPU, no network, no external dependencies, no data. Runnable in seconds on the provided CPU environment (Python 3.14.4).
  - This is a DESIGN only: nothing has been executed, and no results above are measured — they are the analytical predictions the experiment is intended to confirm.

=====================================================================
9. ASSUMPTIONS (separate from fixed task requirements)
=====================================================================
  ASSUMPTIONS:
    A1. The four methods follow standard published ZB semantics (no repo code exists to inspect).
    A2. Backward = 2× forward (B = 2F).
    A3. Communication/transfer cost = 0 (or identical constant) across all methods so it does not confound the schedule comparison.
    A4. "Throughput" = tokens/sec = (M·L)/makespan with F=1; MFU is not used (would require a FLOPs model).
    A5. ZB-2p is modeled at its bubble-free ideal (MS=3M). A more detailed sim could add a small O(1) constant; the ≥90% flatness criterion still holds for small constants relative to M.
    A6. The M-increase trend is evaluated at fixed p and fixed F.
  FIXED TASK REQUIREMENTS (from researcher):
    R1. Grid: M ∈ {2,4,8,16,32}, p ∈ {4,8,16}, F=1, L fixed.
    R2. Metrics: throughput=(M·L)/makespan (F=1), plus normalized throughput (1/makespan) and bubble fraction.
    R3. Success criterion: (a) monotonic non-decreasing in M for 1F1B/1F1B-I/ZB-1p; (b) ZB-2p(M=2) ≥ 90% of ZB-2p(M=32); other three improve >20% over M=2→32.
    R4. Pure-Python dependency-free discrete-event simulation, runnable in seconds.
    R5. Design-only; do not claim any experiment was executed.

=====================================================================
10. UNCERTAINTIES
=====================================================================
  U1. Exact ZB-paper variant (e.g., precise interleaving in ZB-2p, virtual-stage factor V in 1F1B-I) is not pinned down without the source; §3 constants may need adjustment if actual code is provided.
  U2. If the intended repo defines "throughput" differently (steps/sec, MFU), the metric mapping in §5 changes but the experimental framework is unchanged.
  U3. Whether a nonzero fixed comm cost should be modeled could shift absolute makespan values (not the relative ordering or the M-trends).
  U4. ZB-1p's residual-bubble term ((p-1)/M) is an idealization; the exact residual form is uncertain but any term shrinking in M preserves the monotonic-improvement conclusion.
